verdict.rationale: The evidence shows GitHub ships protected branches and code owners on paid plans (comm-16/17). It also has GitHub Actions for automating custom workflows in the repository, and a PR flow where changes get reviewed for quality and security before merge. Nothing documents how protected branches enforce required checks or block merges, so only thin, indirect support exists for enforcing custom merge checks. Missing for 10: first-party docs on required status checks or rulesets that block PR merges, a way to make custom Actions checks mandatory, org-wide compliance enforcement, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can enforce custom quality and compliance merge checks on pull requests

citations.quote: protected branches, draft PRs, Pages, wikis, code owners, multiple assignees, auto review assignment, and scheduled reminders
Automate, customize, and execute your software development workflows right in your repository with GitHub Actions.
A change can start as an issue, be picked up by an agent, return as a pull request, get reviewed for quality and security, and be merged.
